courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary each semester.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Strategies for Social Good: From Analysis to Action
courses.description: This course focuses on social, economic, and structural factors that create and contribute to problems in daily living and explores solutions to foster positive social change. Using social work perspectives, students will engage in reflective assignments, social issue analysis, and solution-identification related to urgent human needs, strengthening communities, and promoting well-being.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Families in Focus: Navigating Challenges, Inspiring Change
courses.description: This course examines the social, economic, and policy issues shaping the lives of children and families in North Carolina and beyond. Using a Person-in-Environment framework, students will explore interventions at the micro, mezzo, and macro levels to address social complexities and promote family well-being. Through reflective assignments, case studies, group projects, and policy discussions, students will gain an in-depth look at the intersection of policy, practice, and advocacy while connecting students to contemporary issues affecting families.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Human Development in Context I: Infancy to Adolescence
courses.description: This course provides an overview of child and adolescent development in an environmental context, using a social work lens to analyze major theoretical frameworks.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Social Work and Systems of Change
courses.description: Through personal reflexivity and historical/systemic analysis, this course examines dynamics of institutional barriers through a critical theory lens. Students explore implications for social work practice, including professional complicity and resistance.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Human Development in Context II: Adulthood
courses.description: This course provides an overview of adult development in environmental and systemic contexts, using social work approaches to the analysis of major developmental frameworks.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Foundations For Evidence-Based Practice & Program Evaluation I
courses.description: This course introduces students to the foundational principles of social work research and evidence-based practice. Through critical engagement with research literature, students will learn how to identify, evaluate, and apply empirical evidence to inform ethical and effective social work interventions. Emphasis is placed on research design, community-engaged methods, and the role of data in advancing social work practice. Students will develop core skills in literature review, peer collaboration, and research communication, preparing them for evidence-informed social work practice.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Foundational Aspects of Engagement and Interviewing
courses.description: This course explores foundational theories, concepts, and skills related to engagement with individuals, groups, communities, and organizations. Emphasis will be placed on building rapport, reflexivity, critical discourse and dialogue, demonstrating cultural humility, and establishing professional helping relationships across micro, mezzo, and macro levels.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Social Welfare Systems and Policies
courses.description: Explores the US social welfare system and its implications for social work practice. Social welfare policies are analyzed, yielding implications for advocacy and action.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: From Classroom to Community: Developing Competencies for Practicum Education
courses.description: This course prepares students for successful social work practicum experiences by integrating theory and practice through reflection, skill-building, and community-engaged learning.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, SOWO 300, SOWO 301, SOWO 315, and SOWO 330.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Social Work Study Abroad
courses.description: Variable content. Course examines international social issues, programs, and policies and their impact on client populations and cultures in a particular country or global region.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Social Work Study Abroad: Africa
courses.description: Course examines social issues, development strategies, health/mental health programs. Explores how country's fledgling democracy and people are redesigning organizations and interventions to respond to the needs of South Africans.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Foundations for Evidence-Based Practice & Program Evaluation II
courses.description: This course introduces students to the key components of evaluating interventions, which is necessary for evidence-based practice. These concepts include the scientific method, human ethics, development of research questions, measurement, and quantitative and qualitative analysis. Students will apply the concepts learned in this course to design their own evaluation project of a social work intervention.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Undergraduate Social Work Practicum
courses.description: In the undergraduate social work practicum, students practice social work knowledge, values, skills, and cognitive and affective processes within a variety of human service settings.

courses.description: Course examines the role of volunteer involvement and citizen participation in community development, grassroots organizing, advocacy, and other efforts to create a more just and democratic society. Includes a service-learning requirement.

courses.description: This course is intended for students who know no Spanish or so little that they feel the need to start over. Students with more than two semesters of college Spanish are not eligible. The course covers the curriculum of first-semester Spanish taught within a health context, with a focus on speaking.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Intermediate Spanish for Health Care I
courses.description: This intermediate course is the equivalent of the third semester of college Spanish. Students will hone their listening and speaking skills in class primarily through role-playing activities and class discussion. Activities center on an original film set in a health clinic in rural North Carolina.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Advanced Spanish for Health Care I
courses.description: Required preparation, third semester Spanish or equivalent. This advanced course reviews the grammar of the third and fourth semester of college Spanish. Students hone their listening and speaking skills through role-playing activities and class discussion. Activities center on an original film set in a Latino-run health clinic.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Treatment Foundation for Problematic Substance Use and Process Addictions
courses.description: Introduces students to the field of problematic substance use and process addiction. Explores historic and current theories of addiction, the key domains of addiction counseling, and applicable ethical and legal considerations.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Human Development in Context
courses.description: This course provides an overview of human development in an environmental context, surveying major theoretical frameworks and highlighting the impact of different systems on the development, functioning and health of individuals, families and communities. Course frameworks will include definitions, structural variations, theories, strengths, stressors, and changes that affect functioning needed to carry out practice with clients.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Mental Health Recovery and Psychiatric Rehabilitation
courses.description: The concept of mental health recovery is introduced, exploring theoretical foundations and lived experiences of consumers. Psychiatric rehabilitation is discussed as a framework and set of interventions supporting recovery.

courses.subject: SOWO

courses.description: This course teaches practical skills for behavioral health care delivered in primary care settings. In this course you will develop expertise in providing brief interventions as part of an interprofessional care team.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Community Organizing
courses.description: In this course, students will learn and apply the universal skills of community change and broad-based community organizing. Students will learn and practice the skills needed to effectively organize communities.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Facilitation Skills Within the Organizational and Community Context
courses.description: Building from group relations theory, this course develops facilitation skills (e.g., agenda setting, process checking, participatory planning, navigating conflict) to engage culturally diverse task group members to achieve identified objectives.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Autism and Neurodiversity-Affirming Practice
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the core vulnerabilities faced by autistic and neurodivergent individuals. Selected neurodiversity-affirming evidence-based interventions will be reviewed with ASD across contexts. Disability and social justice issues faced by this population will be discussed throughout the course.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy
courses.description: This course will use the cognitive behavioral therapy CBT framework to teach students how to move from an assessment to intervention using the CBT model.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Behavioral Intervention with Children
courses.description: This course teaches basic principles of behavior theory and intervention, current applications, and how to assess, design and implement behavior plans for children.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Interpersonal Psychotherapy
courses.description: This practice course focuses on interpersonal psychotherapy, an empirically supported intervention for depression in adolescents and adults. Adaptations for other mental health disorders are discussed.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Differential Diagnosis of Mental Health Disorders
courses.description: This course focuses on the process of conducting a differential diagnosis of mental health and substance use disorders using the current Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Clinical Practice with Addictive Disorders
courses.description: Students develop knowledge, skills, and attitudes specific to clinical practice with clients experiencing Addictive Disorders. This will include effective interventions in a variety of clinical settings utilizing evidence-based and evolving best-practice methodologies.

courses.description: This course facilitates students' acquisition of the knowledge, skills, and attitudes necessary to effectively use 12 common trauma-informed practice elements in interventions for and the treatment of traumatized children and their families. The course highlights consideration of the impact of trauma, intervention objectives, and the practice elements needed to accomplish the intervention objectives. This course is taught using an inquiry-based learning (IBL) pedagogy to enhance students' engagement and learning using full-length cases that exemplify the diverse clients a clinician might encounter in practice.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Approaches to Brief Treatment
courses.description: This advanced practice elective course covers theories and application of three models of brief psychotherapy. Skill building, critical thinking, and utilization of empirical support are emphasized.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Treatment of Trauma and Violence
courses.description: This course focuses on the assessment and treatment of trauma and the impact of violence within the biopsychosocial context. You will learn foundation skills for intervening in direct practice settings with diverse client populations.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Care of the Dying and Bereaved
courses.description: This interdisciplinary clinical course addresses issues and practice models relating to terminal illness and bereavement faced throughout the life span.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Community Organizing
courses.description: This comprehensive course explores the fundamentals and advanced strategies of community organizing, blending theoretical knowledge with practical application. Students will learn to analyze power dynamics and engage in effective community-led public action. The curriculum covers relational power, strategic planning, policy advocacy, and ethical considerations, preparing students with skills to engage in sustained grassroots change.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Child Welfare Perspectives and Practices
courses.description: Focus on the knowledge, skills, and critical thinking necessary for effective practice in child welfare. Students examine their own perspectives regarding pertinent research, current events, and initiatives in the state.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Cognitive Behavior Therapy and Dialectical Behavior Therapy: Essential Practices
courses.description: This course offers an introductory exploration of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) and Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), delving into their theoretical foundations and practical implementation within each model.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, SOWO 540; Pre- or corequisite, SOWO 740.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Administrative and Management: Theory and Practice
courses.description: This course explores contemporary theories, models, and practices for managing human service organizations, emphasizing skills in human resources, leadership, fund management, program implementation, partnerships, equity, organizational change, stakeholder engagement and cultural humility.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, SOWO 500, 505, and 570; Pre- or corequisite, SOWO 740 or SOWO 770.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Interorganizational and Community-Level Theory and Practice
courses.description: This course focuses on social planning, intervention design, and implementation within a complex inter-organizational environment. Theoretical frameworks and historical, sociopolitical and economic contexts of human service delivery systems are discussed.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Sustainable Development
courses.description: Examines perspectives and models of sustainable development. Students will analyze a project and present a participatory plan for engaging in sustainable development work.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Development Theory and Practice in Global Settings
courses.description: This course is designed to assist students to learn skills, methods, theory, and research in development practice in global settings. Focus is on competent practice with marginalized populations globally.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, SOWO 500, 505, and 570; Pre- or corequisite, SOWO 740 or 770.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Marketing and Fundraising for Nonprofit Organizations
courses.description: This course helps students to develop skills and practices associated with marketing and fundraising strategies for nonprofit organizations at the macro level.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Leadership in Nonprofit Organizations
courses.description: An in-depth analysis of the executive role in nonprofit organizations, particularly in leadership transitions, strategic planning, board development, policy administration, governance, employee relations, and resource planning and acquisition.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Financial Management of Nonprofit Organizations
courses.description: Provides basic financial skills for leaders of nonprofits, including bookkeeping fundamentals, interpreting financial statements, budgeting, cash management and investment, and legal compliance.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Program Design and Proposal Development and Pre-implementation Planning
courses.description: Students will learn to develop proposals to fund programs and interventions that address an organizational or social problem or condition and build skills in problem theory, program theory, proposal development, and pre-implementation assessment and planning.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Conceptualizing Social Problems to Inform Interventions
courses.description: An application and critical analysis of behavioral and social science theories and theory- driven research for understanding the etiology of social problems for purposes of social intervention.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Research Methods in Social Intervention
courses.description: An introduction to the basic principles of research for planning and evaluating social interventions. Topics include problem formulation, design, measurement, analysis, and the application of findings to theory and practice.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Introduction to Social Statistics and Data Analysis
courses.description: Designed to explore basic principles and to provide advanced instruction in data analysis, including the construction and analysis of tables, statistical tests, and an introduction to the use of computer programs.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Research Practicum I
courses.description: Students develop independent research competence through work on a research project under the direction of an experienced researcher.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Advanced Research Methods in Social Intervention
courses.description: Students build advanced competence in research design, data collection, data analysis, and statistics by analyzing exemplary social work research and presenting independent learning projects within specialized areas of study.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Measurement in Intervention Research
courses.description: This course focuses on the development of knowledge and skills in measuring social, psychological, environmental, and other factors related to intervention with individuals, families, groups, and organizations.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Research Practicum II
courses.description: Continuation of Research Practicum I.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Structural Equation Modeling
courses.description: SEM is a general statistical method that can be employed to test theoretically derived models. In this course, students will learn fundamental concepts and skills to conduct SEM, and how to apply these techniques to social work and related areas of research.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Longitudinal and Multilevel Analysis
courses.description: This course introduces the context and intuition for longitudinal and multilevel models, and the statistical frameworks, analytical tools, and social behavioral applications of multilevel modeling (MLM) and longitudinal analysis.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Applied Regression Analysis and Generalized Linear Models
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. This course introduces statistical frameworks, analytical tools, and social behavioral applications of OLS regression model, weighted least-square regression, logistic regression models, and generalized linear models.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Special Topics in Doctoral Research
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Topic determined by instructor and announced in advance.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Special Topics in Social Work Doctoral Studies
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Topic determined by the instructor and announced in advance.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Qualitative Analysis
courses.description: This course will introduce the application of qualitative research methods for social work research.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Causal Inference for Social Work Research
courses.description: This course focuses on topics and methods for causal inference in social work research.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Systemic Reviews and Introduction to Meta-Analysis
courses.description: This course focuses on conducing and writing systematic reviews in social work and related behavioral/social sciences, as well as an introduction to meta-analysis.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Professional Development Seminar: Navigating Doctoral Studies and Beyond
courses.description: This seminar-style course seeks to bolster the explicit and implicit curriculum of preparing social work scholars. The course focuses on preparing students for a successful doctoral education experience and individual development of their scholarly identities. The course will also introduce students to specialized knowledge and skills that will allow them to develop and implement a program of research in their future careers. This course is required for first year doctoral students in the School of Social Work. Other doctoral students are welcome to attend sessions of interest with permission from the instructor.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Development of Social Intervention Models
courses.description: This PhD-level course focuses on preparing advanced graduate students with the knowledge and skills needed to design and develop interventions that address social needs, problems, and conditions.

courses.subject: SOWO
courses.title: Teaching Practicum
courses.description: This practicum provides a range of supervised classroom or training opportunities designed to prepare advanced doctoral students for faculty positions in undergraduate- and graduate-level social work education.
